solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beginning of play being performed: start filming!

parts.note: the first act of a play is Act I, written ACT I
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: A theatre direction blending into a film director's cry as the curtain rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of play' looks like a first-letter pick, but it is the opening act, ACT I.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director calls 'Action!' to tell cast and crew that shooting begins.

clue.text: Cheat doubly to get US apartment

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them
a second word for cheat: to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A shady deal that swindles twice over to land an American flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' asks for cheat a second time, in a different word: CON, then DO.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a condo, short for condominium, is an apartment owned by its occupant.

clue.text: Uncouth bride collapses, having drunk two litres

indicators.note: the rearranged bride takes in the litres as a drinker takes in liquor
something that collapses falls apart, so the letters of bride are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre, so two litres are LL

explanation.surface: A bride overdoes it at the reception and falls down, which looks rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapses' signals the anagram, and 'having drunk' signals the insertion, as a drinker takes liquor in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-bred has poor manners from a bad upbringing, so is uncouth.

clue.text: Grandmother makes bread

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a grandmother
..., also spelt naan, is a flat Indian bread

explanation.surface: Granny is in the kitchen baking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a familiar name for a granny and a South Asian flatbread.

clue.text: Not very clean food to hand

parts.note: grub is slang for food
something to hand is by you, close at hand

explanation.surface: Snacks left within reach that are a little grimy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means dirty or grimy, so somewhat lacking in cleanliness.

clue.text: Wreathed with flowers, a fish out of water?

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a landed fish has been hauled out of the water

explanation.surface: A floral image followed by a hint of a fish flapping on the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a fish out of water' reads as the idiom for someone ill at ease, but it splits into a fish and its catching.
explanation.definitionFit: To be garlanded is to be decked with a wreath or chain of flowers.

clue.text: Dark lake surrounded by military group

indicators.note: the lake's letter sits within the military group's word

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers
L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: Soldiers camped round a lake at night with no lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere unlit has no lights on, so it is dark.

clue.text: Bravo! Help for member of the band

parts.note: Bravo is B in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to assist is to help

explanation.surface: Applause for a musician who helps the group along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo!' looks like a cheer but is the radio code word for B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist plays bass guitar or double bass, a regular part of a group of musicians.

clue.text: Just a single ship? That's a joke

parts.note: just a single one, numerically one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a navy of only one vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a quip told in a single sentence, a short gag.

clue.text: Beat the Spanish horse

parts.note: las is a Spanish word for the (feminine plural)
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone whipping a horse in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is not a mount but the drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to strike with a whip, so to beat.

clue.text: In favour of enclosing University Square

indicators.note: the word for in favour of wraps round the letter for university

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for

explanation.surface: Supporting a plan to wall in a college quadrangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a campus quad, but it is the number: four is two squared.
explanation.definitionFit: Four is a square number, being two multiplied by itself.

clue.text: Tips for hot weather clothing cease to convince

definitions.meaning: advice on summer dress would be to ... things
an excuse that wears thin loses its persuasive power

explanation.surface: Fashion advice for summer alongside a comment on a stale argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an excuse or joke growing weaker with repetition until nobody believes it.

clue.text: From list of bequests, one at a time sons cut out by choice

parts.note: a will lists what a person leaves to heirs

indicators.note: the sons are removed from the word for one at a time

parts.note: singly means one by one
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A father writes his sons out of his will deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut out' looks like disinheriting, but it removes S from SINGLY, leaving INGLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something willingly means doing it voluntarily, of your own accord.

clue.text: Composer's name announced

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a handle is slang for a person's name

explanation.surface: A composer's name being read out at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name' looks like part of the definition, but it is the slang word HANDLE, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel wrote Messiah and the Water Music.

clue.text: Missed stroke, as atmosphere's sweltering

parts.note: air is the atmosphere, and 's adds S
sweltering means very hot

explanation.surface: A golfer misses the ball in stifling heat.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket an air shot is a swing that fails to touch the ball.

clue.text: Beyond delta, soil shortage

indicators.note: soil's word comes after the delta letter

parts.note: Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
earth is soil

explanation.surface: Past a river delta, farmland grows scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delta' looks like a river mouth but is the code word for D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: Patriarch putting an undergarment over back of thigh

indicators.note: in a down entry the bra piece sits above the ham piece

parts.note: an gives A
a bra is an undergarment
the ham is the back of the thigh

explanation.surface: Someone pulling on underwear over a leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham is the founding father of the Israelites in Genesis, the first of the biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Wild dancing in red fez

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so in red fez is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dancing frantically while wearing a red fez.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenzied means frantic and uncontrolled, as in a wild rush.

clue.text: Hotel in French city is just the place for me

indicators.note: the hotel's letter goes inside the French city's name

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a hotel on the Riviera ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position ideally suited to someone.

clue.text: Cathedral on right bank

indicators.note: in an across entry the cathedral's word is placed after the right's letter

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: A cathedral standing on the right bank of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverside but is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on or trust them.

clue.text: What's in large bottle? Some swill it: retsina!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A toast urging drinkers to knock back Greek wine from a big bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Big bottles of wine or soft drink are often sized at one litre, a metric measure of volume.

clue.text: After dinner treat some munch occasionally

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A post-meal sweet to nibble now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' looks like an alternate-letter pick, but only a hidden run works.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc, short for chocolate, is a sweet often served after a meal.

clue.text: Breaking par, eight lead

indicators.note: breaking the words apart lets their letters be reassembled

explanation.surface: A golfer goes under par and takes an eight-shot lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a golf lead but is the pencil material.
explanation.definitionFit: Pencil lead is actually graphite, a soft form of carbon.

clue.text: Remains sort of blonde

definitions.meaning: ... blonde is a pale greyish hair colour

explanation.surface: A pale-haired type stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means burnt residue and also a greyish shade of fair hair.

clue.text: Knowing about shirt being really tough

indicators.note: the word for knowing goes round the shirt

parts.note: a sly look is a knowing one
a tee is a T-shirt

explanation.surface: A wry remark about a shirt that wears like armour.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and unyielding like steel, as in steely resolve.

clue.text: Impede the movement of basket

definitions.meaning: a large lidded basket, as for picnics

explanation.surface: A cumbersome basket gets in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for hindering and a wicker container for food.
